title: Rabbi Abba Serungiya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He appears in aggadah in Jerusalem Talmud Sukkah 4:3 and Bereshit Rabbah 1:6. Bamidbar Rabbah 14:4 calls him Sidrungiya; Rashash already notes there that it should be Serungiya. Bamidbar Rabbah 22:8 has Rabbi Abba of Romanya, and the same statement in Tanchuma, Matot 7, is attributed to Rabbi Abba Sangoriya. Eichah Rabbah 1:41 has Rabbi Biba of Marungiya; at the end of section 51 it has Rabbi Biba Sangoriya. Pesikta Rabbati, in the section “Bayom,” has Rabbi Abba Sarungla. Hyman considers these forms the name of one Amora, called after his town: Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3 and Ketubot 12:3 mention the ancient synagogue of Serungin.

notes.text: The spelling forms Sidrungiya, Serungiya, Romanya, Sangoriya, Marungiya, Sarungla and Serungin remain distinct. Hyman treats them as one town-derived name. ססנ״א is read as “end of section 51,” not as an otherwise unidentified commentator.

The consulted Bamidbar Rabbah 22:8 names Abba of Romanya. The equations among Serungiya, Sidrungiya, Sangoriya, Marungiya and Sarungla, and the explanation from a town, are Hyman’s proposals, not identities established here.
